title: Grade 4 ELA — Making Inferences from Evidence
subject: English Language Arts
description: Practice with questions on clues, character, setting, text evidence.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Bo slipped a card into his sister's bag and grinned. He had hidden the crayons when she walked in. What can you infer Bo is planning?
Bo slipped a card into his sister's bag and grinned. He had hidden the crayons when she walked in. Which clue most supports that idea?
choices: He slipped a card into her bag.

questions.question: All the seats were folded up except one row. A hand-lettered sign said “Rehearsal.” A violin case rested by the stage. What will most likely happen soon?
choices: The stage will become a swimming pool.
The seats will all be sold.

questions.question: All the seats were folded up except one row. A hand-lettered sign said “Rehearsal.” A violin case rested by the stage. Which pair of details best supports the inference?
choices: the folded seats and the case color
the rehearsal sign and violin case

questions.question: Ezra came in with cool cheeks and wet boots. He put his gloves by the heater. What can you infer about the weather outside?
choices: It is probably hot and dry.
It is probably cold and wet.
It is probably warm and windy only.

questions.question: Nora read each instruction twice. When the first corner would not fit, she carefully folded it again. How does Nora seem to approach the task?
choices: by giving up as soon as possible

questions.question: Overnight the river rose over the lowest trail. At sunrise a worker carried a rope and a CLOSED sign to its entrance. Why will the worker probably put the rope across the trail?
choices: to keep visitors away from flooded ground
to measure the length of a boat
to hold a sign open in strong sun

questions.question: Sam had practiced his speech with his brother many times. Outside the classroom, his notes shook in his hand. How does Sam most likely feel before speaking?
choices: certain that he will fall asleep

questions.question: Ina heard a steady tap inside the sink cabinet. A puddle was spreading beneath a pipe. What is likely happening?
choices: The tap sound is from the stairs.
Someone put ice inside the cabinet.

questions.question: A hiker brushed leaf litter aside and pointed to a line of rinsed stones and a mud mark above the bank. What most likely happened before the hike?
choices: The leaves fell up from the ground.

questions.question: By the time class began, Max's desk partner had an extra pencil and a clean eraser. Max had brought two of each. Why did Max most likely bring extras?
choices: to share with someone who might need them

questions.question: A bent gate leaned open. The seed tray beyond it was empty, and tiny footprints crossed the dirt. What is one reasonable inference about the seed tray?
choices: A small animal may have eaten the seeds.
The footprints were made by a bus.
The seeds flew to the Moon.

questions.question: On the way to the recital, Eli tapped a rhythm against his knee and hummed the beginning of a tune. What might Eli be doing?
choices: checking how long the road is

questions.question: Before trying the ramp, Tali checked each bolt and asked her teammate to hold the base. Which word best describes Tali's approach?
After recess, Sol dried a bench before setting down the class notebooks. Umbrellas stood open near the door. What most likely happened earlier?
choices: The umbrellas were used as pencils.

questions.question: The grass in the marked square was just as tall as outside it. The gardener wrote “not yet” on the chart and set another date to check. What was the gardener probably waiting to see?
choices: a visible difference in grass growth

questions.question: Jin put the wide wheels back on after the cart got stuck in loose sand with narrow wheels. What does Jin probably think will help?
choices: using wheels that sink less in sand
putting more sand on the path

questions.question: Before dinner, Meera checked two bowls and moved the tiny one beside the dog's bed. What can you infer the tiny bowl might be for?
“We still have ten minutes,” Ren said, but kept glancing at the clock and hurrying through his work. What do Ren's actions suggest?
choices: He wants the room to get darker.
He hopes to work all night.

questions.question: The note on the garden bed read, “These are too small this week. Please wait to pick them.” Small green tomatoes hung from the vines. What does the writer expect?
choices: The tomatoes will grow and ripen later.
The note will make tomatoes change color right away.
The tomatoes are ready to pick now.
The vines will be moved indoors today.
